```text
  Piece Movement Logic (Knight and Archer)

  Knight: Moves in an L shape (two squares in one direction, one in the orthogonal direction). However, unlike Western
  chess, it can be blocked by an adjacent piece in its primary direction of movement (similar to the Horse in Chinese
  chess). Specifically, if the Knight moves 2 squares horizontally and 1 square vertically, the blocking square is at
  ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y); if it moves 1 square horizontally and 2 squares vertically, the blocking
  square is at (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2). The move is invalid if any piece occupies this intermediate
  square.

  Archer: Moves any distance orthogonally without jumping. For non-capturing moves, the path between source and
  destination must be completely clear (no pieces in between). For capturing moves, there must be exactly one piece (of
  any color) between the source and destination, which serves as the "screen" or "mount" for the capture (similar to the
   Cannon in Chinese chess).

  Move Generation: Each piece generates candidate moves from its current position, then filters them by applying global
  and piece-specific validation rules.

  Piece Labels: Knight displays as 'K', Archer displays as 'A'.

  Rule Validation System (Rule Implementations)

  Global Rules: Source must not be vacant (VacantRule), source and destination must differ (NilMoveRule), source and
  destination must be within board limits (OutOfBoundaryRule), and destination cannot contain a friendly piece
  (OccupiedRule).

  Protection Rule: During the first numMovesProtection turns of the game, no piece can be captured
  (FirstNMovesProtectionRule). The protection phase also prevents win condition evaluation.

  Piece-Specific Rules: Knight moves must conform to its L shape and blocking constraints (KnightMoveRule,
  KnightBlockRule). Archer moves must conform to its orthogonal sliding and jumping capture constraints
  (ArcherMoveRule).KnightMoveRule and KnightBlockRule are only applied to moves generated by Knight pieces. ArcherMoveRule is only applied to moves generated by Archer pieces. Moves from other piece types are not subject to piece-specific rules.

  Board Display and Coordinates

  The board uses a coordinate system where columns are labeled with letters (a, b, c, ...) and rows are labeled with
  numbers (1, 2, 3, ...), both starting from the bottom-left corner. User input format is "source->destination" (e.g.,
  "a1->b2"). Empty squares display as '.', and the central square (when empty) displays as 'x'. Pieces display with
  their color and label (e.g., a red Knight displays as a red 'K').
  Internal board representation contract: The board is stored as board[x][y] (x =column, y = row, both 0-based from                                                  
  bottom-left). All reads/writes must go through Game.getPiece(...) (and              
  Game.setPiece(...) if applicable). Direct indexing into board[][] in piece/rule code is forbidden.
  ConsolePlayer Input Contract
  ConsolePlayer.nextMove(Game game, EList<Move> availableMoves) receives the
  already-computed legal moves for the current player. It does not need to parse
  board-coordinate move strings such as "a1->b2".
  
  ConsolePlayer must read one line from System.in and interpret it as a zero-based
  integer index into availableMoves. Input "0" selects availableMoves.get(0),
  input "1" selects availableMoves.get(1), and so on. A valid index satisfies 0 <= index < availableMoves.size().

  External Knowledge and Tools

  The following infrastructure classes and tools are already fully implemented in the project but are NOT included in
  the Ecore model. You can invoke them directly when generating code:

  MoveRecord: An independent data class that records a player and their move, with methods such as getPlayer() and
  getMove(). It is available as a utility type (not required by the current JesonMor core loop).

  InvalidConfigurationError: A custom error class located in assignment.protocol.exception. Throw this when encountering
   invalid initialization parameters.
```

# Operation Specifications
Knight::getAvailableMoves
Summary: Generates all candidate Knight L-shaped moves from the given source
         square, then filters them through the global rule pipeline. The
         KnightBlockRule is applied separately as a piece-specific check.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
  2. For each of the eight L-shaped offsets
     {(±1, ±2), (±2, ±1)}:
       a. Compute destination = (source.x + dx, source.y + dy).
       b. If destination is outside the board, skip.
       c. Create a Move(source, destination).
       d. Validate the move using all global rules (VacantRule,
          NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule) AND
          KnightMoveRule (L-shape) AND KnightBlockRule (no piece in the
          "leg's knee" square).
       e. If all validations pass, add the Move to the candidate list.
  3. Return the candidate list.
Related Features: Source Place passed as parameter; result list of Moves.
Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, VacantRule, NilMoveRule,
                 OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, KnightMoveRule,
                 KnightBlockRule.
Input:
  - game: Game - the current game context for querying board state.
  - source: Place - the square holding the Knight; must be within board.
Output:
  - List<Move> - candidate Knight moves that pass all applicable rules.
Pre-condition: The Knight piece occupies the source square; the Game board
               is initialized.
Post-condition: The board state is unchanged; a fresh list is returned.

  public Player start()
  {

      Piece piece = getPiece(chosenMove.getSource());

          break;

      currentPlayer = other;
      setCurrentPlayer(currentPlayer);
    }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Determines the winner of the game based on the board state and
   *          the last move executed, applying the central-place, capture, and
   *          score-comparison rules while respecting the protection phase.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If game.numMoves <= configuration.numMovesProtection, return null
   *      (no winner can be declared during the protection phase).
   *   2. Check the "Knight leaves the central square" condition:
   *        - If lastPiece is a Knight, lastMove.source equals
   *          configuration.centralPlace, and lastMove.destination does NOT equal
   *          configuration.centralPlace, return lastPlayer as the winner.
   *   3. Check the "only one player's pieces remain" condition:
   *        - Scan the board via Game.getPiece(...). Count pieces belonging to
   *          each player.
   *        - If at least one player has zero pieces remaining and the other has
   *          at least one, return the player that still has pieces.
   *   4. If neither above condition holds and the current player has no
   *      available moves (game.getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer) is empty),
   *      compare scores:
   *        - If lastPlayer.score > otherPlayer.score, return lastPlayer.
   *        - If lastPlayer.score < otherPlayer.score, return the other player.
   *        - If scores are equal, return lastPlayer (current player wins on tie).
   *   5. Otherwise (game is still ongoing), return null.
   * Related Features: board (queried via Game.getPiece); configuration.
   * Related Classes: Game, Player, Piece, Knight, Move, Place, Configuration.
   * Input:
   *   - lastPlayer: Player - the player who just executed the move.
   *   - lastPiece: Piece - the piece that was moved.
   *   - lastMove: Move - the move that was just executed.
   * Output:
   *   - Player - the winning player, or null if the game has not yet ended.
   * Pre-condition: lastPlayer and lastPiece correspond to a move that has just
   *                been applied; configuration and board are consistent.
   * Post-condition: No state is modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public Player getWinner(final Player lastPlayer, final Piece lastPiece, final Move lastMove)
  {
    Configuration config = getConfiguration();
    if (getNumMoves() <= config.getNumMovesProtection())
    {
      return null;
    }
    // Check "Knight leaves the central square" condition
    if (lastPiece instanceof Knight && lastMove != null
        && lastMove.getSource() != null && lastMove.getSource().equals(config.getCentralPlace())
        && (lastMove.getDestination() == null || !lastMove.getDestination().equals(config.getCentralPlace())))
    {
      return lastPlayer;
    }
    // Check "only one player's pieces remain" condition
    Player survivingPlayer = null;
    boolean multipleWithPieces = false;
    for (Player p : config.getPlayers())
    {
      boolean hasPiece = false;
      Piece[][] board = getBoard();
      for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++)
      {
        for (int j = 0; j < board[i].length; j++)
        {
          Piece pc = board[i][j];
          if (pc != null && pc.getPlayer() == p)
          {
            hasPiece = true;
            break;
          }
        }
        if (hasPiece) break;
      }
      if (hasPiece)
      {
        if (survivingPlayer == null)
        {
          survivingPlayer = p;
        }
        else
        {
          multipleWithPieces = true;
          break;
        }
      }
    }
    if (survivingPlayer != null && !multipleWithPieces)
    {
      return survivingPlayer;
    }
    // Check the "no available moves" condition for score comparison
    if (getAvailableMoves(lastPlayer).isEmpty())
    {
      // Find the other player
      Player otherPlayer = null;
      for (Player p : config.getPlayers())
      {
        if (p != lastPlayer)
        {
          otherPlayer = p;
          break;
        }
      }
      if (lastPlayer.getScore() >= otherPlayer.getScore())
      {
        return lastPlayer;
      }
      else
      {
        return otherPlayer;
      }
    }
    return null;
  }

  public void updateScore(final Player player, final Piece piece, final Move move)
  {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int manhattanDistance = Math.abs(source.getX() - destination.getX())
                          + Math.abs(source.getY() - destination.getY());
    player.setScore(player.getScore() + manhattanDistance);
  }

  /**

   * <!-- end-user-doc -->

   * Summary: Executes a move on the board by relocating the piece from the

   *      destination (capturing any existing piece, which is overwritten).
   *   4. Set Game.setPiece(move.source, null) to clear the source square.
   *   5. Increment game.numMoves by 1.
   * Related Features: board (mutated via Game.setPiece), numMoves (incremented).
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece.

   *           Places and the source must contain a piece.
   * Output: void.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - The move has already been validated and is legal under all rules.
   *   - move.source is within board limits and holds a non-null piece.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The source square is null.
   *   - The destination square holds the moved piece.
   *   - game.numMoves has been incremented by 1.

  public void movePiece(final Move move)
  {

    setPiece(move.getSource(), null);

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Computes the complete list of legal moves available to the given
   *          player for the current board state, combining per-piece candidate
   *          generation with the global rule validation pipeline.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty result list.
   *   2. For each Place on the board:
   *        a. Read the piece at that square via Game.getPiece(place).
   *        b. If the piece is null, skip.
   *        c. If piece.player != given player, skip.
   *        d. Call piece.getAvailableMoves(game, place) to obtain candidate
   *           moves for that piece.
   *        e. For each candidate Move, run the full rule pipeline (global
   *           rules + FirstNMovesProtectionRule + piece-specific rules such as
   *           KnightMoveRule / KnightBlockRule / ArcherMoveRule as appropriate).
   *        f. If all validations pass, add the Move to the result list.
   *   3. Return the result list.
   * Related Features: board (queried via Game.getPiece); result list of Move.
   * Related Classes: Game, Piece, Knight, Archer, Move, Place, VacantRule,
   *                  NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule,
   *                  FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule,
   *                  ArcherMoveRule, Player.
   * Input:
   *   - player: Player - the player whose legal moves are being requested.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - every legal move (source, destination) available to the
   *     given player. The list may be empty if the player has no legal moves.
   * Pre-condition: The board and configuration are initialized; player is one of
   *                the players in configuration.players.
   * Post-condition: The board state is unchanged; the returned list is a freshly
   *                 allocated collection.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
  {
    EList<Move> result = new BasicEList<Move>();
    Piece[][] board = getBoard();
    // Global rules
    Pa20Factory factory = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE;
    VacantRule vacantRule = factory.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = factory.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = factory.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = factory.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = factory.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    firstNMovesProtectionRule.setNumProtectedMoves(getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection());
    // Piece-specific rules
    KnightMoveRule knightMoveRule = factory.createKnightMoveRule();
    KnightBlockRule knightBlockRule = factory.createKnightBlockRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = factory.createArcherMoveRule();

    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++)
    {
      for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++)
      {
        Place place = factory.createPlace();
        place.setX(x);
        place.setY(y);
        Piece piece = getPiece(place);
        if (piece == null) continue;
        if (piece.getPlayer() != player) continue;
        EList<Move> candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
        for (Move move : candidates)
        {
          if (!outOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!vacantRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!nilMoveRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!occupiedRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          boolean pieceSpecificValid = true;
          if (piece instanceof Knight)
          {
            if (!knightMoveRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
            if (!knightBlockRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
          }
          else if (piece instanceof Archer)
          {
            if (!archerMoveRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
          }
          if (!pieceSpecificValid) continue;
          result.add(move);
        }
      }
    }
    return result;
  }

   *        b. If the piece is null, skip.
   *        c. If piece.player != given player, skip.
   *        d. Call piece.getAvailableMoves(game, place) to obtain candidate
   *           moves for that piece.
   *        e. For each candidate Move, run the full rule pipeline (global
   *           rules + FirstNMovesProtectionRule + piece-specific rules such as
   *           KnightMoveRule / KnightBlockRule / ArcherMoveRule as appropriate).
   *        f. If all validations pass, add the Move to the result list.
   *   3. Return the result list.
   * Related Features: board (queried via Game.getPiece); result list of Move.
   * Related Classes: Game, Piece, Knight, Archer, Move, Place, VacantRule,
   *                  NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule,
   *                  FirstNMovesProtectionRule, KnightMoveRule, KnightBlockRule,
   *                  ArcherMoveRule, Player.
   * Input:
   *   - player: Player - the player whose legal moves are being requested.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - every legal move (source, destination) available to the
   *     given player. The list may be empty if the player has no legal moves.
   * Pre-condition: The board and configuration are initialized; player is one of
   *                the players in configuration.players.
   * Post-condition: The board state is unchanged; the returned list is a freshly
   *                 allocated collection.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Player player)
  {
    EList<Move> result = new BasicEList<Move>();
    Piece[][] board = getBoard();
    // Global rules
    Pa20Factory factory = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE;
    VacantRule vacantRule = factory.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = factory.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = factory.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = factory.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = factory.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    firstNMovesProtectionRule.setNumProtectedMoves(getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection());
    // Piece-specific rules
    KnightMoveRule knightMoveRule = factory.createKnightMoveRule();
    KnightBlockRule knightBlockRule = factory.createKnightBlockRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = factory.createArcherMoveRule();

    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++)
    {
      for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++)
      {
        Place place = factory.createPlace();
        place.setX(x);
        place.setY(y);
        Piece piece = getPiece(place);
        if (piece == null) continue;
        if (piece.getPlayer() != player) continue;
        EList<Move> candidates = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
        for (Move move : candidates)
        {
          if (!outOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!vacantRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!nilMoveRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!occupiedRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          boolean pieceSpecificValid = true;
          if (piece instanceof Knight)
          {
            if (!knightMoveRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
            if (!knightBlockRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
          }
          else if (piece instanceof Archer)
          {
            if (!archerMoveRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
          }
          if (!pieceSpecificValid) continue;
          result.add(move);
        }
      }
    }
    return result;
  }

} // JesonMor

```java
   *          given source square by enumerating orthogonal sliding destinations in
   *          four directions, then filtering them through the global rule pipeline
   *          and the ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
   *   2. For each of the four orthogonal directions (dx, dy) in
   *      {(1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)}:
   *        a. Initialize screenCount = 0 (no screen encountered in this direction).
   *        b. Walk step by step starting from (source.x + dx, source.y + dy) while
   *           the position is inside the board:
   *             i.   Get the piece at the current position via Game.getPiece(...).
   *             ii.  If the position is empty:

   *                     and destination = current. Validate the move using all
   *                     global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule,
   *                     OccupiedRule) AND ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass,
   *                     add the Move to the candidate list.
   *                   - If screenCount > 0: This position cannot be a valid
   *                     destination (path is not clear for non-capturing, and
   *                     there is no piece to capture). Skip and continue walking.
   *             iii. If the position has a piece (any color):
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: This piece is the screen. Set
   *                     screenCount = 1. Continue walking in this direction.
   *                   - If screenCount == 1: This piece is the destination. Create
   *                     a Move with source = source and destination = current.
   *                     Validate the move using all global rules AND
   *                     ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass, add the Move to
   *                     the candidate list. Then stop scanning this direction.
   *   3. Return the candidate list.
```

```java
   *          given source square by enumerating orthogonal sliding destinations in
   *          four directions, then filtering them through the global rule pipeline
   *          and the ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
   *   2. For each of the four orthogonal directions (dx, dy) in
   *      {(1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)}:
   *        a. Initialize screenCount = 0 (no screen encountered in this direction).
   *        b. Walk step by step starting from (source.x + dx, source.y + dy) while
   *           the position is inside the board:
   *             i.   Get the piece at the current position via Game.getPiece(...).
   *             ii.  If the position is empty:
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: Create a Move with source = source
   *                     and destination = current. Validate the move using all
   *                     global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule,
   *                     OccupiedRule) AND ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass,
   *                     add the Move to the candidate list.
   *                   - If screenCount > 0: This position cannot be a valid
   *                     destination (path is not clear for non-capturing, and
   *                     there is no piece to capture). Skip and continue walking.
   *             iii. If the position has a piece (any color):
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: This piece is the screen. Set
   *                     screenCount = 1. Continue walking in this direction.
   *                   - If screenCount == 1: This piece is the destination. Create
   *                     a Move with source = source and destination = current.
   *                     Validate the move using all global rules AND
   *                     ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass, add the Move to
   *                     the candidate list. Then stop scanning this direction.
   *   3. Return the candidate list.
   * Related Features: Source Place passed as parameter; result list of Move objects.
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, VacantRule, NilMoveRule,
   *                  OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, ArcherMoveRule.
   * Input:
   *   - game: Game - the current game context used to query board state via
   *           Game.getPiece(...).
   *   - source: Place - the square from which the Archer is generating moves; must
   *             contain this Archer piece and be within board limits.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - a list of Move objects whose source = the Archer's current
   *     position and whose destination is a legally reachable square. The list
   *     may be empty if the Archer has no legal moves.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - The Archer piece is placed at the given source square.
   *   - The Game is in a valid state with a fully initialized board.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The returned list contains only moves that pass every applicable global
   *     rule and the ArcherMoveRule. No board state is mutated.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated
   */
  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
```

```java
  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Generates all legal candidate moves for an Archer piece located at the
   *          given source square by enumerating orthogonal sliding destinations in
   *          four directions, then filtering them through the global rule pipeline
   *          and the ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
   *   2. For each of the four orthogonal directions (dx, dy) in
   *      {(1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)}:
   *        a. Initialize screenCount = 0 (no screen encountered in this direction).
   *        b. Walk step by step starting from (source.x + dx, source.y + dy) while
   *           the position is inside the board:
   *             i.   Get the piece at the current position via Game.getPiece(...).
   *             ii.  If the position is empty:
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: Create a Move with source = source
   *                     and destination = current. Validate the move using all
   *                     global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule,
   *                     OccupiedRule) AND ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass,
   *                     add the Move to the candidate list.
   *                   - If screenCount > 0: This position cannot be a valid
   *                     destination (path is not clear for non-capturing, and
   *                     there is no piece to capture). Skip and continue walking.
   *             iii. If the position has a piece (any color):
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: This piece is the screen. Set
   *                     screenCount = 1. Continue walking in this direction.
   *                   - If screenCount == 1: This piece is the destination. Create
   *                     a Move with source = source and destination = current.
   *                     Validate the move using all global rules AND
   *                     ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass, add the Move to
   *                     the candidate list. Then stop scanning this direction.
   *   3. Return the candidate list.
   * Related Features: Source Place passed as parameter; result list of Move objects.
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, VacantRule, NilMoveRule,
   *                  OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, ArcherMoveRule.
   * Input:
   *   - game: Game - the current game context used to query board state via
   *           Game.getPiece(...).
   *   - source: Place - the square from which the Archer is generating moves; must
   *             contain this Archer piece and be within board limits.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - a list of Move objects whose source = the Archer's current
   *     position and whose destination is a legally reachable square. The list
   *     may be empty if the Archer has no legal moves.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - The Archer piece is placed at the given source square.
   *   - The Game is in a valid state with a fully initialized board.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The returned list contains only moves that pass every applicable global
   *     rule and the ArcherMoveRule. No board state is mutated.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```

public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
{
    EList<Move> candidates = new BasicEList<Move>();
    int size = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule();
    
    for (int[] dir : directions)
    {
        int dx = dir[0];
        int dy = dir[1];
        int screenCount = 0;
        int x = source.getX() + dx;
        int y = source.getY() + dy;
        while (x >= 0 && x < size && y >= 0 && y < size)
        {
            Piece piece = game.getPiece(x, y);
            if (piece == null)
            {
                if (screenCount == 0)
                {
                    Move move = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
                    move.setSource(source);
                    Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
                    destination.setX(x);
                    destination.setY(y);
                    move.setDestination(destination);
                    if (vacantRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        nilMoveRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        occupiedRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        archerMoveRule.validate(game, move))
                    {
                        candidates.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
            else
            {
                if (screenCount == 0)
                {
                    screenCount = 1;
                }
                else
                {
                    Move move = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
                    move.setSource(source);
                    Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
                    destination.setX(x);
                    destination.setY(y);
                    move.setDestination(destination);
                    if (vacantRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        nilMoveRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        occupiedRule.validate(game, move) && 
                        archerMoveRule.validate(game, move))
                    {
                        candidates.add(move);
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
            x += dx;
            y += dy;
        }
    }
    return candidates;

   * Summary: Generates all legal candidate moves for an Archer piece located at the
   *          given source square by enumerating orthogonal sliding destinations in
   *          four directions, then filtering them through the global rule pipeline
   *          and the ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
   *   2. For each of the four orthogonal directions (dx, dy) in
   *      {(1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)}:
   *        a. Initialize screenCount = 0 (no screen encountered in this direction).
   *        b. Walk step by step starting from (source.x + dx, source.y + dy) while
   *           the position is inside the board:
   *             i.   Get the piece at the current position via Game.getPiece(...).
   *             ii.  If the position is empty:
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: Create a Move with source = source
   *                     and destination = current. Validate the move using all
   *                     global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule,
   *                     OccupiedRule) AND ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass,
   *                     add the Move to the candidate list.
   *                   - If screenCount > 0: This position cannot be a valid
   *                     destination (path is not clear for non-capturing, and
   *                     there is no piece to capture). Skip and continue walking.
   *             iii. If the position has a piece (any color):
   *                   - If screenCount == 0: This piece is the screen. Set
   *                     screenCount = 1. Continue walking in this direction.
   *                   - If screenCount == 1: This piece is the destination. Create
   *                     a Move with source = source and destination = current.
   *                     Validate the move using all global rules AND
   *                     ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass, add the Move to
   *                     the candidate list. Then stop scanning this direction.
   *   3. Return the candidate list.
   * Related Features: Source Place passed as parameter; result list of Move objects.
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece, VacantRule, NilMoveRule,
   *                  OutOfBoundaryRule, OccupiedRule, ArcherMoveRule.
   * Input:
   *   - game: Game - the current game context used to query board state via
   *           Game.getPiece(...).
   *   - source: Place - the square from which the Archer is generating moves; must
   *             contain this Archer piece and be within board limits.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - a list of Move objects whose source = the Archer's current
   *     position and whose destination is a legally reachable square. The list
   *     may be empty if the Archer has no legal moves.
   * Pre-condition:
   *   - The Archer piece is placed at the given source square.
   *   - The Game is in a valid state with a fully initialized board.
   * Post-condition:
   *   - The returned list contains only moves that pass every applicable global
   *     rule and the ArcherMoveRule. No board state is mutated.

  public EList<Move> getAvailableMoves(final Game game, final Place source)
  {
    EList<Move> candidates = new BasicEList<Move>();
    int size = game.getConfiguration().getSize();
    int[][] directions = {{1, 0}, {-1, 0}, {0, 1}, {0, -1}};
    VacantRule vacantRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createOccupiedRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createArcherMoveRule();

    for (int[] dir : directions)
    {
      int dx = dir[0];
      int dy = dir[1];
      int screenCount = 0;
      int x = source.getX() + dx;
      int y = source.getY() + dy;
      while (x >= 0 && x < size && y >= 0 && y < size)
      {
        Piece piece = game.getPiece(x, y);
        if (piece == null)
        {
          if (screenCount == 0)
          {
            Move move = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
            move.setSource(source);
            Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
            destination.setX(x);
            destination.setY(y);
            move.setDestination(destination);
            if (vacantRule.validate(game, move) &&
                nilMoveRule.validate(game, move) &&
                outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, move) &&
                occupiedRule.validate(game, move) &&
                archerMoveRule.validate(game, move))
            {
              candidates.add(move);
            }
          }
        }
        else
        {
          if (screenCount == 0)
          {
            screenCount = 1;
          }
          else
          {
            Move move = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createMove();
            move.setSource(source);
            Place destination = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE.createPlace();
            destination.setX(x);
            destination.setY(y);
            move.setDestination(destination);
            if (vacantRule.validate(game, move) &&
                nilMoveRule.validate(game, move) &&
                outOfBoundaryRule.validate(game, move) &&
                occupiedRule.validate(game, move) &&
                archerMoveRule.validate(game, move))
            {
              candidates.add(move);
            }
            break;
          }
        }
        x += dx;
        y += dy;
      }
    }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Enforces the Chinese-chess-style "horse leg" blocking rule: a
   *          Knight cannot move if a piece occupies the intermediate "knee"
   *          square along its primary direction of travel.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Retrieve source and destination Places from the Move.
   *   2. If the move is not L-shaped (i.e., not one of the eight standard
   *      offsets), return true (the L-shape check is KnightMoveRule's job; this
   *      rule does not block non-L moves).
   *   3. Determine the "knee" square:
   *        - If the move is 2 steps horizontal + 1 step vertical, the knee is
   *          ((source.x + destination.x) / 2, source.y).
   *        - If the move is 1 step horizontal + 2 steps vertical, the knee is
   *          (source.x, (source.y + destination.y) / 2).
   *   4. If Game.getPiece(knee) returns a non-null piece, return false
   *      (blocked).
   *   5. Otherwise return true.
   * Related Features: None (stateless rule).
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece.
   * Input:
   *   - game: Game - used to read the knee square via Game.getPiece(...).
   *   - move: Move - the candidate Knight move.
   * Output:
   *   - boolean - true if the knee square is empty (or the move is non-L), false
   *               if a piece blocks the knee.
   * Pre-condition: move.source and move.destination form a valid L-shape.
   * Post-condition: No state is modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int dx = Math.abs(destination.getX() - source.getX());
    int dy = Math.abs(destination.getY() - source.getY());
    
    // Check if the move is L-shaped: must be (2,1) or (1,2)
    boolean isHorizontalL = (dx == 2 && dy == 1);
    boolean isVerticalL = (dx == 1 && dy == 2);
    
    if (!isHorizontalL && !isVerticalL)
    {
      return true;
    }
    
    int kneeX;
    int kneeY;
    if (isHorizontalL)
    {
      // 2 horizontal + 1 vertical: knee is at midpoint of x, same y as source
      kneeX = (source.getX() + destination.getX()) / 2;
      kneeY = source.getY();
    }
    else
    {
      // 1 horizontal + 2 vertical: knee is same x as source, midpoint of y
      kneeX = source.getX();
      kneeY = (source.getY() + destination.getY()) / 2;
    }
    
    if (game.getPiece(kneeX, kneeY) != null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    
    return true;

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Validates whether a proposed move is a legal move for an Archer piece
   *          by checking orthogonal sliding constraints (clear path for non-
   *          capture, exactly-one-screen for capture).
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Retrieve the source and destination Places from the Move.
   *   2. If source and destination are not aligned horizontally or vertically
   *      (i.e., exactly one of dx, dy is non-zero), return false.
   *   3. Compute the unit step (sdx, sdy) toward the destination.
   *   4. Walk from the square adjacent to source toward destination, counting the
   *      number of intermediate pieces encountered (the "screen" count).
   *   5. Determine whether destination holds a piece:
   *      - If destination is empty (non-capture): screen count must be 0
   *        (path must be clear).
   *      - If destination is occupied (capture): screen count must be exactly 1,
   *        i.e., exactly one piece (any color) lies between source and
   *        destination.
   *   6. Return true if the screen-count condition is satisfied, false otherwise.
   * Related Features: None (stateless rule).
   * Related Classes: Game, Move, Place, Piece.
   * Input:
   *   - game: Game - used to read intermediate and destination squares via
   *           Game.getPiece(...).
   *   - move: Move - the candidate move whose source must contain the Archer and
   *           whose destination is the target square.
   * Output:
   *   - boolean - true if the move is a legal Archer move; false otherwise.
   * Pre-condition: The Move has valid source and destination Places; the Game
   *                board is initialized.
   * Post-condition: No state is modified.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean validate(final Game game, final Move move)
  {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int dx = destination.getX() - source.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY() - source.getY();

    // The move must be exactly horizontal or vertical: one of dx, dy is zero
    // and the other is non-zero.
    if ((dx == 0) == (dy == 0))
    {
      return false;
    }

    int sdx = Integer.signum(dx);
    int sdy = Integer.signum(dy);

    // Walk from the square adjacent to source toward destination (excluding
    // destination) and count the number of intermediate pieces encountered.
    int screen = 0;
    int cx = source.getX() + sdx;
    int cy = source.getY() + sdy;
    while (cx != destination.getX() || cy != destination.getY())
    {
      if (game.getPiece(cx, cy) != null)
      {
        screen++;
      }
      cx += sdx;
      cy += sdy;
    }

    // If destination is empty (non-capture), the path must be clear.
    // If destination is occupied (capture), exactly one piece must screen it.
    Piece destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);
    if (destPiece == null)
    {
      return screen == 0;
    }
    else
    {
      return screen == 1;
    }
  }

```java
   *          four directions, then filtering them through the global rule pipeline
   *          and the ArcherMoveRule.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
   *   2. For each of the four orthogonal directions (dx, dy) in
   *      {(1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)}:
   *        a. Initialize screenCount = 0 (no screen encountered in this direction).
   *        b. Walk step by step starting from (source.x + dx, source.y + dy) while

   *                     and destination = current. Validate the move using all
   *                     global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule,
   *                     OccupiedRule) AND ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass,
   *                     add the Move to the candidate list.

   *                     destination (path is not clear for non-capturing, and
```

```java
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. Initialize an empty candidate list.
   *   2. For each of the four orthogonal directions (dx, dy) in
   *      {(1,0), (-1,0), (0,1), (0,-1)}:

   *        b. Walk step by step starting from (source.x + dx, source.y + dy) while

   *             ii.  If the position is empty:

   *                     and destination = current. Validate the move using all
   *                     global rules (VacantRule, NilMoveRule, OutOfBoundaryRule,
   *                     OccupiedRule) AND ArcherMoveRule. If all validations pass,
   *                     add the Move to the candidate list.
   *                   - If screenCount > 0: This position cannot be a valid
   *                     destination (path is not clear for non-capturing, and
```

1. Compute context information

  1.2 Also consider the related classes in the Javadocs.
  1.3 Locate these files in your project.
  1.4 Generate the class summarization.
2. Read the error messages carefully.
3. Do your best to fix the errors locally without introducing new types, fields, and methods.
4. You should not remove faulty methods to eliminate compilation errors.
5. Do not change parts without errors.

## EMF Coding Style
- When possible, call getter/setter methods to access field values. Do not read/write raw fields derived from the class diagram.
- The getter of a boolean attribute `bv` looks like `isBv()`, e.g., `isIsTrue()` for `isTrue`.
- When possibe, use the creation factory for object creation.
- To create an EList instance, import and use `org.eclipse.emf.common.util.BasicEList`.

```java
   *        b. If the piece is null, skip.

   * Input:
   *   - player: Player - the player whose legal moves are being requested.
   * Output:
   *   - List<Move> - every legal move (source, destination) available to the

   * Pre-condition: The board and configuration are initialized; player is one of

   * Post-condition: The board state is unchanged; the returned list is a freshly

    Pa20Factory factory = Pa20Factory.eINSTANCE;
    VacantRule vacantRule = factory.createVacantRule();
    NilMoveRule nilMoveRule = factory.createNilMoveRule();
    OutOfBoundaryRule outOfBoundaryRule = factory.createOutOfBoundaryRule();
    OccupiedRule occupiedRule = factory.createOccupiedRule();
    FirstNMovesProtectionRule firstNMovesProtectionRule = factory.createFirstNMovesProtectionRule();
    firstNMovesProtectionRule.setNumProtectedMoves(getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection());
    // Piece-specific rules
    KnightMoveRule knightMoveRule = factory.createKnightMoveRule();
    KnightBlockRule knightBlockRule = factory.createKnightBlockRule();
    ArcherMoveRule archerMoveRule = factory.createArcherMoveRule();

        place.setY(y);

            if (!knightBlockRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;

          else if (piece instanceof Archer)
          {

          }
          if (!pieceSpecificValid) continue;
          result.add(move);
        }
      }
    }
```

```java
        place.setX(x);
        place.setY(y);
        Piece piece = getPiece(place);
        if (piece == null) continue;
        if (piece.getPlayer() != player) continue;

        for (Move move : candidates)
        {
          if (!outOfBoundaryRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!vacantRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!nilMoveRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!occupiedRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          if (!firstNMovesProtectionRule.validate(this, move)) continue;
          boolean pieceSpecificValid = true;
          if (piece instanceof Knight)
          {
            if (!knightMoveRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
            if (!knightBlockRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
          }
          else if (piece instanceof Archer)
          {
            if (!archerMoveRule.validate(this, move)) pieceSpecificValid = false;
          }
          if (!pieceSpecificValid) continue;
          result.add(move);
        }
      }
    }
    return result;
  }
```
